mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met, or the trigger fires but returns are not statistically different from baseline (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the negative correlation between GDPC1 decline and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate above 4.0% within a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 4.0% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower after the trigger compared to baseline (p > 0.10), or the trigger fires but returns are positive more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its previous 12-month maximum for three consecutive months signals an acceleration in economic output and capacity utilization, which supports higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO exceeds 12-month max for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher after the trigger compared to baseline (p > 0.05), or the trigger occurs but returns are negative more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and CPI inflation above 2.0% for two consecutive months signals a dual shock of higher interest rates and inflation, eroding corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2.0% and CPIAUCSL > 2.0% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower when both proxies exceed thresholds, or positive returns occur in more than 50% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months indicates a broad-based weakening in demand, which depresses earnings expectations and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower when both proxies decline together, or positive returns occur in more than 50% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its previous 12-month maximum for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS exceeds 12-month maximum for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher after the trigger, or positive returns occur in fewer than 40% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between real personal income (proxied by RSAFS) growth and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, such that higher-than-average monthly income growth predicts positive SPX returns within the short horizon.
failure_condition: The correlation between monthly RSAFS growth and subsequent 5-day SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.10) or is negative in more than 60% of rolling 12-month windows.
